quote: Section 2.2 provides for automatic renewal for successive five-year terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal "not more than 270 days and not less than 240 days before the expiration of the Initial Term." That window was approximately **June 3 – June 23, 2026**. ... If no notice was given, the Agreement will **automatically renew for five years** (through February 28, 2032)
reason: The memo identifies the right problem in Supply Agreement § 2.2: automatic renewal for successive five-year terms, with non-renewal only by notice within the 270-to-240-day band. It explains the consequence for Harrowgate, which is being locked into five more years with exclusivity and the amended terms attached. It also recommends calendaring the next window, shortening renewals and simplifying non-renewal. This matches the ledger's expected finding. One flaw: the memo never says 'a 30-day window' outright, and it misdates the window. It gives June 3 – June 23 (about 20 days), when 240 days before Feb 28, 2027 is about July 3, 2026. Because it quotes the exact 270/240 language and treats the window as narrow and already missed, it still captures the issue in substance.
